chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever says these words at every prescribed prayer, he will be protected in his self, his house, his wealth, and his children.

I seek refuge for myself, my wealth, my children, my family, my house, and everything that is mine, with Allah the One, the Unique, the Eternal, who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.
And I seek refuge for myself, my wealth, my children, and everything that is mine, with the Lord of Daybreak, from the evil of what He has created, up to its end.
And with the Lord of Mankind, up to its end.
And with the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), up to its end.

key_terms.آيَةِ الْكُرْسِيِّ: The Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for protection after obligatory prayers in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith prescribes a comprehensive protective dhikr recited after every obligatory prayer, emphasizing the preservation of the self, family, wealth, and home through divine refuge. It uniquely integrates the recitation of Surah Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas, and Ayat al-Kursi as a unified spiritual shield, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating Quranic recitation with daily ritual practice. This practice underscores the belief in the tangible spiritual protection afforded by specific divine attributes and verses in safeguarding against both visible and invisible harms.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Aziz, from Bakr Bin Muhammad, from the one who reported it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who says these words during every Prescribed Salāt, there would be Protection regarding himself, and his house, and his wealth, and his children, and the wife and all what he owns:

‘I seek Refuge for myself, and my children, and my wealth, and my children, and my family, and my house, and everything what is from me, with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the One, the First, the Last, who neither begets nor is begotten, and there does not happen to be anyone as a match for Him<sup>azwj</sup>.
And I seek Refuge for myself, and my wealth, and my children, and everything what is from me, with [113:1] the Lord of Al-Falaq, [113:2] From the evil of what He has Created – up to its end,
and with [114:1] Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the people – up to its end,
and Ayat Al Kursy [2:255] – up to its end’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz from Bakr ibn Muhammad from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Whoever says these words with every obligatory prayer will receive protection for his own soul, his home, his belongings and children:

‘I seek refuge for myself, belongings, children, family, home and everything of me with Allah, the One and only Self- sufficient Who has not given birth to anyone nor is born from anyone and there is no one like Him.

‘I seek refuge [for myself, belongings, children and all that is of me] with the Lord of the opening dawn from the evil of that which He has created, . . .’ recite to the end of Chapter 113 of the Holy Quran,
